cards.q: What is the RP (Rendezvous Point) in PIM-SM?
cards.a: The RP is the router where receivers' (*,G) joins meet the source's register traffic; it is the hub of PIM-SM. Every PIM-SM router must know the group-to-RP mapping.

cards.q: What tasks does the RP perform for a PIM-SM group?
cards.a: Receivers join (*,G) toward it, the source's FHR registers to it, and shared-tree traffic flows through it; routers depend on the group-to-RP mapping.

cards.q: What are the three ways to learn the group-to-RP mapping?
cards.a: Static (manual ip pim rp-address), Auto-RP (Cisco proprietary, dynamic), and BSR (PIM draft standard, vendor-neutral). Static is the simplest and an exam favorite; Auto-RP and BSR provide dynamic mapping and redundancy.

cards.q: How does Auto-RP discover and distribute RP mappings?
cards.a: Candidate RPs send RP-announcements to the RP-discovery agent, which maps and distributes them, and a mapping agent picks the winner by election based on IP or weight, with the highest RP IP typically winning ties.

cards.q: How does BSR distribute RP mappings?
cards.a: An elected bootstrap router (BSR) receives announcements from candidate RPs and floods the resulting mapping to all PIM routers; election favors the highest priority/IP.

cards.q: Which commands configure static, Auto-RP, and BSR RP mapping?
cards.a: Static: ip pim rp-address <IP>; Auto-RP: ip pim send-rp-announce Loopback0 scope 32 and ip pim send-rp-discovery Loopback0 scope 32; BSR: ip pim bsr-candidate Loopback0 0 and ip pim rp-candidate Loopback0.

cards.q: What are the RP placement and redundancy strategies?
cards.a: A central RP is simple but a single point of failure; anycast RP uses a shared loopback plus MSDP for redundancy and shared load; per-group RP gives control over scale.

cards.q: Which commands verify RP mapping and configuration?
cards.a: show ip pim rp mapping, show ip pim rp hash, show ip pim neighbor, and show ip mroute; debug ip pim auto-rp for Auto-RP issues.

cards.q: No RP mapping is being learned; what do you check?
cards.a: Whether static or auto announcements are configured and reaching the routers; verify with show ip pim rp mapping.

cards.q: Multicast traffic is flowing via the wrong RP; what do you check?
cards.a: An RP mapping conflict; run show ip pim rp hash to see how the group hashes to an RP.

cards.q: Auto-RP shows no mappings; what is missing?
cards.a: Both the announce and discovery functions with proper scope; check with show ip pim rp mapping and debug ip pim auto-rp.

cards.q: Which groups does Auto-RP use, and what is the catch?
cards.a: Auto-RP uses 224.0.1.39 and 224.0.1.40; these groups are Cisco proprietary and considered legacy.

cards.q: What happens if there is no RP for a PIM-SM group?
cards.a: No shared tree can be built, so PIM-SM cannot operate for that group; every PIM-SM router must have the group-to-RP mapping.
